chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding the man who buys the slave girl or marries her.
Without rishdah (maturity/prudence), and he takes her for himself, so he (peace be upon him) said: If he does not fear the defect (of illegitimacy) upon his children, then there is no problem.

key_terms.الْعَيْبَ: Defect or flaw, here referring to a legal or social defect such as illegitimacy (bastardy) affecting the offspring.
key_terms.رِشْدَةٍ: Maturity or prudence, often referring to mental or financial maturity in legal contexts.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a slave girl who lacks maturity (rishdah)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam clarifies the permissibility of marrying or acquiring a slave girl lacking *rishdah* (maturity/discretion), noting that the primary concern is not the mother's status itself but whether it might result in a specific legal defect (*'ayb*) for the offspring. This reflects the Shia juristic focus on lineage purity and the practical implications of maternal status on the child's social and legal standing within the community.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) regarding the man who buys the slave girl or marries her
without the right way, and he takes her for himself. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he does not fear the shame upon his children, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ’Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about the case of a man who buys a slave-girl or marries her
without proper wedlock and keeps her for his own self, he (the Imam) has said, ‘If he is not afraid of the stigma for his children, it is not unlawful.”’
